definitions.gloss: highest-ranking courtesan; oiran of the top rank
definitions.explanation: The most elite rank of courtesan in Edo-period pleasure quarters, distinguished by exceptional beauty, cultural refinement, and artistic accomplishments.

definitions.gloss: lead performer; master narrator or puppeteer
definitions.explanation: A title for high-ranking performers in traditional Japanese arts, especially the lead chanter in bunraku puppet theater and certain Noh performers.

notes:
An important term in Japanese cultural history with two distinct but related meanings. Both senses share the idea of being at the top of a hierarchy.

Also written as {大夫|たゆう}. The alternate reading だゆう exists but たゆう is standard.

ETYMOLOGY:
The courtesan sense dates to the Edo period (1603-1868). {太夫|たゆう} were the elite of the pleasure quarters, particularly {吉原|よしわら} in Edo and {島原|しまばら} in Kyoto. Unlike lower-ranking courtesans, they could refuse clients and were celebrated for their cultural accomplishments. The {太夫|たゆう} rank gradually disappeared by the mid-Edo period as the ⟦{花魁|おいらん}→花魁：15374_oiran⟧ system replaced it.

The performer sense remains alive in ⟦{文楽|ぶんらく}→文楽：13156_bunraku⟧ (bunraku puppet theater), where the {太夫|たゆう} is the chanter who narrates the entire story.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{花魁|おいらん}→花魁：15374_oiran⟧: oiran — high-ranking courtesans who succeeded the {太夫|たゆう} system
- ⟦{遊女|ゆうじょ}→遊女：16645_yuujo⟧: courtesan; prostitute — the general term for women in the pleasure quarters
- ⟦{語|かた}り{手|て}→語り手：14271_katarite⟧: narrator — a general term for a storyteller in any context
